# The inline tab header band stays a gradient in the neo themes

## Context

The `ui: 'inline'` design pass for dock tab headers (#17950 variants, #17963 header actions, #18043 title weight and trim, #18048) left one value untouched: the header's band. `theme-neo-dark/tab/Container.scss:10-14` and its neo-light twin value `--tab-header-inline-background-image` as a 180° gradient from `--sem-color-surface-neutral-highlighted` to `--sem-color-surface-neutral-default` — in neo-dark that resolves to gray-800 `#292D28` → gray-900 `#0E0F0D`, an olive-tinted ramp; in neo-light to white → `#fafafa`. `src/tab/Container.scss:1-7` paints it (`&.neo-tab-container-inline > .neo-tab-header-toolbar { background-image: var(--tab-header-inline-background-image, none) }`), and the header owns nothing else: `src/tab/header/Toolbar.scss:2` is `background-color: transparent`, no border, no color token.

The operator (2026-09-02) saw the ramp on a consumer's dock panes and named it as not fitting the app; he had assumed the inline pass flattened it. It did — for one app. `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss:74-84` re-values the hook with the Workstation's own two panel colors and explains why: *"The neo themes value this hook with a neutral olive ramp; painted over this instrument's blue-slate panel it read as a foreign surface"* — then sets the header's `background-color` longhand and a `border-bottom` line separately (`:196-204`), noting the shorthand fights the engine rule. The flagship app rejects the default; every other host inherits it.

Sibling, same family (defaults lag the apps' overrides): #18080 — the engine's default reveal chrome vanishes on a dark ground while the Workstation and the cockpit override it.

## The Problem

The default should be the good default. A consumer that adopts `enableDock*Action` and `ui: 'inline'` gets the engine's density and action chrome for free, then still has to discover one token to stop the band reading as a gradient over its surfaces — and has NO token at all for the header's own color or its separating line, because the inline header carries neither. The Workstation's answer (its own palette + longhand background + border) is the shape the theme should offer as its baseline: a flat header surface and a hairline, valued from semantic tokens, with the gradient hook kept for consumers who want one.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/tab/Container.scss:1-14` and `resources/scss/theme-neo-light/tab/Container.scss:10-14` — the inline band token; the same sheets already carry the inline density tier (`--tab-button-height: var(--sem-height-large)` etc.).
- `resources/scss/src/tab/Container.scss:1-7` — the variant selector that paints the band; the comment there names it "the public inline-header hook".
- `resources/scss/src/tab/header/Toolbar.scss:2` — the toolbar's own paint is transparent; actions (`:12-49`) keep their tokens.
- `resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/design-tokens/Semantic.scss:18,31,32` — `--sem-color-border-default: var(--gray-700)`, `--sem-color-surface-neutral-default: var(--gray-900)`, `--sem-color-surface-neutral-highlighted: var(--gray-800)`; neo-light `:18,31,32` — gray-200, gray-50, white.
- `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss:70-84, 196-204` — the Workstation's override (its own palette; stays).
- `buildScripts/util/check-theme-coverage.mjs` — values must land in BOTH neo themes.
- Screenshots that contain an inline header: `test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DockPinCollapseNL.spec.mjs:281-315` (eight darwin `reveal-pin-<theme>-{enabled,disabled}.png`, re-recorded by PR #18090 for #18089 today); `test/playwright/visual/PreviewLanguageVisual.spec.mjs:115,131` (to be checked at implementation).

## The Fix

1. Both neo themes (`tab/Container.scss`, same block that owns the inline tokens): `--tab-header-inline-background-image: none` (the hook stays a public token — consumers who want a gradient keep valuing it); add `--tab-header-inline-background-color: var(--sem-color-surface-neutral-highlighted)` and `--tab-header-inline-box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 var(--sem-color-border-default)`.
2. `src/tab/Container.scss` inline rule paints the header from those tokens with transparent fallbacks, so the legacy themes and every other host stay byte-identical: `background-color: var(--tab-header-inline-background-color, transparent)`, the existing `background-image` hook, and the hairline as `box-shadow: var(--tab-header-inline-box-shadow, none)` — one whole-value token (a colour-inside-a-fixed-shadow fallback still computes to a transparent shadow STRING on the legacy themes, not `none`), an inset shadow, NOT `border-bottom`, so the header's box does not grow by a pixel under the zero-gap geometry (#18015) and no height-asserting spec moves.
3. Workstation: its override keeps winning on its own palette; the comment that calls the theme value an olive ramp is corrected to name the new baseline.
4. Witness: a component paint spec in the DockRailTabPaint idiom (computed styles on a rendered inline header, both neo themes, with a control): the inline header's `background-image` is `none`, its `background-color` equals the resolved `--sem-color-surface-neutral-highlighted`, the inset line is present — and a standalone (`ui: null`) header keeps its established paint. Red-first on dev: the computed `background-image` is the gradient.
5. Baselines: the eight `DockPinCollapseNL` reveal-pin PNGs show the inline header and change with the band. They are re-recorded in this PR **after** #18090 merges (sequencing: #18090 first, then this), or, if this lands first, #18090's images are re-recorded once more — either way one recording against the final band.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 `theme-neo-dark` and `theme-neo-light` `tab/Container.scss` value `--tab-header-inline-background-image: none`, `--tab-header-inline-background-color` and `--tab-header-inline-box-shadow` from semantic tokens; `check-theme-coverage` stays green.
- [ ] AC-2 `src/tab/Container.scss` paints the inline header's color and inset hairline from the tokens with transparent fallbacks; `theme-dark`, `theme-light`, `theme-cyberpunk` compile to unchanged inline-header paint (no tokens → transparent/none).
- [ ] AC-3 Component paint witness, both neo themes: `background-image` `none`, `background-color` = resolved `--sem-color-surface-neutral-highlighted`, hairline present as the inset shadow; standalone header control unchanged; red-first on dev.
- [ ] AC-4 The Workstation's inline headers are byte-identical before/after (its override wins); its comment names the new baseline.
- [ ] AC-5 `DockPinCollapseNL` reveal-pin baselines recorded against the flat band in the order stated in Fix 5; `PreviewLanguageVisual` checked and re-recorded only if an inline header is in frame.
- [ ] AC-6 `components` + `unit/dashboard` suites green at head.

## Out of Scope

- Brand or overlay themes (a token-only theme riding another theme's sheets) — the primitive a consumer brand theme needs; ideation-sandbox material, not this leaf.
- #18080 (default reveal chrome on a dark ground) — sibling, separate.
- The legacy `theme-dark` / `theme-light` — they carry no inline tokens and keep their paint.
- Promoting the Workstation palette itself into a theme.

## Avoided Traps

- **`border-bottom` for the hairline** — grows the header box by 1 px under the zero-gap geometry and moves every height-asserting spec; the inset `box-shadow` paints the same line at zero layout cost.
- **`background` shorthand** — its implicit `background-image: none` fights the higher-specificity engine rule (the Workstation learned this at `Viewport.scss:196-204`); longhands only.
- **Removing the gradient hook** — consumers (the Workstation included) value it; the default becomes `none`, the token stays public.
- **Re-recording baselines before #18090 lands** — two PRs racing on the same eight PNGs; sequence, record once.

## Related

- #17950, #17963, #18043, #18048 — the inline header design pass this completes.
- #17984 — the Workstation's palette bridge.
- #18080 — sibling: default reveal chrome.
- #18089 / PR #18090 — the reveal-pin baselines this change moves.

* fix(tab): every theme states the inline header's paint, because a fallback is not a reset (#18141)

Switching a running app from a neo theme to a classic one left the `ui: 'inline'`
dock tab header on its dark neo surface, and a consumer had written an in-app
override to compensate.

#18095 / PR #18097 gave the inline header a flat surface plus a hairline by
valuing `--tab-header-inline-background-color` and `--tab-header-inline-box-shadow`
in the two neo themes only, on the premise its own comment states: "a theme that
values nothing (the legacy themes) paints exactly what it painted before".

A `var()` fallback is a default, never a reset. It is reached only when the
property is unset on the element AND every ancestor, and custom properties
inherit from the `:root .neo-theme-*` element that declares them. A theme scope
nested inside another — which `component.Base#getTheme` walks the component chain
to support, and which occurs in a live app because theme classes land on several
elements at once — therefore keeps the OUTER theme's value wherever it declares
nothing of its own. Omitting a token does not opt out of a surface; it opts in to
whatever the nearest declaring ancestor decided.

The counter-statement was already four lines away, on the one token the classic
themes do declare: "this explicit value must not decay into reliance on the
structural fallback". That comment was right and covered one of three siblings.

Both classic themes now state all three explicitly at the flat values they intend,
so the paint is unchanged where no neo ancestor exists and correct where one does.
Separation stays with `--tab-container-content-border`, which both declare. The
neo themes are untouched. The structural comment no longer teaches the premise.

The witness nests deliberately: a classic theme applied to the document alone
reads transparent even while broken, because nothing declares the token and the
fallback covers it — so only an outer scope that DOES value it can prove the inner
one resets.

* test(dashboard): the dock-lock fixture offers both theme families (#18141)

The nested-scope arms need the classic theme stylesheets in the document. With
only the two neo themes configured, adding `neo-theme-light` to an element
declares nothing — no sheet defines `:root .neo-theme-light` — so the toolbar
keeps inheriting the neo surface and the arm fails whether or not the fix is
present. It failed exactly that way before this change: a red that measured an
absent stylesheet rather than the product.

Four themes is also the reported configuration: the defect was found switching a
running app between the neo and classic families, which only an app loading both
can do.

* test(dashboard): the four-theme requirement gets its own fixture (#18141)

The nested arms need the classic theme stylesheets in the document, and my first
pass got that by widening the SHARED dock-lock fixture from two themes to four.
Every other consumer of that fixture then booted two stylesheets it never reads,
and DockLock.spec.mjs is one — its first arm focuses a tab button and clicks it,
which is a focus-gated re-projection race that a slower boot can only widen. It
went red on CI while passing 25/25 locally.

I am NOT claiming that attribution: a re-run of the same SHA is the controlled
experiment, and DockRailLazyModule failed in the same job on a fixture this diff
cannot reach. The change stands on its own merits — a spec's requirement does not
belong on a surface its neighbours share, and one fixture per concern is what the
other twenty do.

dock-theme-nesting reuses dock-lock's app with its own four-theme config, exactly
as dock-static-boot-overlap reuses dock-static-boot's. Two files, no duplicated
app. dock-lock returns to the two themes it had.

Found by @neo-opus-vega while holding the review seat on the red.

* docs(tab): the explicit-hook rule covers the four themes that own a tab sheet (#18141)

The replacement comment said "every theme therefore states all three hooks
explicitly". There is a fifth build target. theme-cyberpunk ships no tab/
directory at all and declares none of these tokens, so a cyberpunk scope nested
inside a neo one still inherits the neo surface — the very defect the sentence
claimed was covered.

That is the same premise-teaching failure this change exists to correct: the
comment it replaced taught the next author that omitting is safe; this one would
have taught them that all of them are handled. Narrowed to the four themes that
own a tab/ sheet, with the fifth named as the known gap it is.

It also restores something the first draft dropped: the fallback is load-bearing
for a theme that ships no sheet at all. ContainerUi.spec.mjs already records that
for the same fifth theme. Both halves are true — a fallback serves a theme that
declares nothing anywhere, and cannot reset one nested inside a theme that does.

Caught by @neo-opus-vega.

* docs(tab): cut the theme-hook comments back to the rule (#18141)

The comment explaining why each theme states its inline hooks had grown into an
essay: the getTheme component-chain walk, the cyberpunk gap, and a restatement of
what inheritance does. None of that belongs beside a CSS declaration.

Kept the rule a reader needs at that line — a fallback is a default, never a
reset, so an omitted property inherits rather than resets. The rest lives in
#18141 and the spec."
